purpose: Execution protocol v1.7 = v1.5 plus the changes listed here. Sections not named here are unchanged from v1.5. evaluation-protocol.json is still the full v1.5 text; v1.5 and older files and results stay unchanged.

provenance.v1.6: Never existed: no commit on any branch contains eval-protocol/v1.6. EVAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION went from v1.5 to v1.7 in b96a9c1.
provenance.prompt_rewrite: Introduced in b96a9c1 (Mac engineering qualification, 2026-11-11). The commit records no rationale, no dev-set result and no model call that motivated it; Q11 states that run added no model calls. Whether earlier LIVE results informed the wording is NOT RECORDED.
provenance.consequence: Treat every task already used with earlier protocol versions as exposed. v1.7 results are not comparable with v1.5 or older results, in either direction.

changes_since_v1.5.system_prompt: EVAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT is one source-first tool-selection prompt shared by every arm: choose the shortest available route to exact source; a tool that returns Java or linked XML source at a known declaration anchor may replace a separate lookup and read; paths, search matches, declaration summaries and reconstructed signatures are locators only; all delivered source consumes one budget. Exact text: scripts/evaluate-java-task.mjs EVAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT.
changes_since_v1.5.java_evidence_tool: The java_evidence declaration describes Java source plus linked MyBatis XML at a candidate's relativePath and selection.line/column, bounded windows for large methods and partial coverage. Exact text: EVAL_JAVA_EVIDENCE_TOOL.
changes_since_v1.5.arms: b0/b1/b2 map to product profiles broad/outline/outline-evidence on one server build (decisions.md D9). java_outline spends no source budget and is never credited as received source.
changes_since_v1.5.index_readiness: On MAC-10 adapter runs (and on any run given --index-ready-timeout-ms N > 0) every product session waits until java_status reports indexView.state FRESH, at most N ms (adapter default 900000; kit runs default 0, i.e. v1.5 timing). The first wait happens before the model loop; the wait after a repair write re-opens the session inside that tool call. Waits are recorded per row as indexReadyMs and are included in elapsedMs, so latency comparisons must subtract them. Control arms open no product session and never wait. A session that cannot become FRESH before the loop is BLOCKED_SETUP; after a write it is SESSION_REBIND_FAILED with the row marked partial. Reason: since b96a9c1 outline answers NOT_READY at once on a cold view, so without the wait B1/B2 would measure cold start, not the tools (06 §6.4 allows a prebuilt backend with its cost reported separately).
changes_since_v1.5.qa_facets: Every QA row also carries answerCorrect and requiredEvidenceCovered (06 §6.5: path coverage and task success are separate facts). taskSuccess still requires both, plus the budget.
changes_since_v1.5.frozen_kit: Rows that are BLOCKED or MISSING in the frozen kit report keep their unmeasured JS outcome.
changes_since_v1.5.identity: --require-identity also hashes the product server file; results packs record evalProtocol, indexReadyTimeoutMs, pilot and the mac10 adapter identity. --inputs/--source-budget on non-MAC-10 rows exit 2.

mac10_adapter.cli: evaluate-java-task.mjs --dataset <dataset-manifest.json> --tasks <tasks-{split}.jsonl> --gold <private/gold-{split}.jsonl> --inputs <frozen inputs.json> --source-budget none|LINES:BYTES [--pilot N --pilot-seed S]; repair tasks need ILV2_TOOLCHAINS (no override flag)
mac10_adapter.refused: --repo-roots, --kit-root and --public-answer-contract with --inputs; mixed MAC-10 and other task rows; MAC-10 rows without --dataset; a LIVE run of MAC-10 rows without --inputs.
mac10_adapter.corpora: Each input checkout must be at its frozen head with no untracked, ignored or modified file (git status --porcelain --ignored); otherwise the run fails closed, because materializeCorpus copies the working tree and build output (classes of the fix or of hidden tests) would reach the agent. Then materializeCorpus (the retrieval runner's): APFS clone without .git, all repair pre-state overlays of that corpus, hidden tests removed, overlay/hidden/evidence hashes checked; one materialized corpus per run under <output>/corpora, copied per attempt. The raw repository is never a corpus.
mac10_adapter.task_text: The task prompt, then 'Named anchors: ...' when the task has anchors (agent-visible by dataset design); for QA also 'Answer rules: ' with the dataset contract's rules, then the public answer keys and fields (a curator slot description, when present, prefixes the generic one). QA tasks receive the source budget sentence only when a budget is set.
mac10_adapter.answer_contract: Taken from the dataset's own answer-contract part (hash pinned by the manifest). Slot types map to public fields: string -> string (minLength 1), string-set -> array of strings (order not scored), boolean, integer.
mac10_adapter.qa_success: strict JSON with exactly the slots; string-set compared as a set (sorted, duplicates fail); every required evidence line received in a dispatched request from the file version the curator verified (file_sha256 = fileContentHash); received source within the run-level budget when one is set. No frozen kit is involved (scorer.kind = mac10-adapter).
mac10_adapter.repair_success: The candidate may change only the oracle's file; any other added, changed or removed file is REJECTED_DISALLOWED_EDIT before the oracle runs; a symlink or directory at the oracle file is REJECTED_NOT_REGULAR_FILE; a deleted file is MISSING_FILE. The repaired file is judged by the MAC-10 oracle (evaluateOracle: javac + java with the frozen JDK of ILV2_TOOLCHAINS, every frozen file under javaHome hash-checked before the run; completion receipt plus ORACLE PASS marker). PASS -> VALIDATED_SUCCESS; JUDGE_ERROR, including any exception inside the judge, keeps the slot unmeasured; every other state is a failure. The oracle test never enters the candidate. The shared native test tool still only compiles builds it supports, the same on every arm.
mac10_adapter.source_budget: Run-level and identical on every arm (06 §6.4). MAC-10 tasks carry no budget of their own, so --source-budget must be given explicitly; 'none' is recorded as null.
mac10_adapter.pilot: --pilot N --pilot-seed S picks N tasks from the split (after --filter) by a deterministic stratified rule over (corpus, category) that never reads gold; the rule and task ids are recorded in identity.pilot.

comparison: Within v1.7 every arm gets the same prompt, native tools and budget; product arms additionally wait for a FRESH index (control arms have no product session). Arms differ only in the product tools of their profile. mac10-v3 dev and its already-viewed holdout are historical regression sets (06 §6.1): a v1.7 result on them cannot claim generalization.
